question: Should Slack get a first-class opt-in outbound DM recipient allowlist config, or should outbound recipient policy remain a plugin/SDK hook capability?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and outbound authorization semantics that overlap existing hook-based policy work and the trusted-operator security model.

options.title: Approve Slack `allowSendTo`/`dmAllowTo`
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in Slack recipient allowlist that preserves current behavior when unset and is enforced in the Slack send path with docs and tests.

options.title: Route Through Plugin Hooks
options.body: Defer Slack config and instead use or extend `message_sending` target context so a ClawHub or npm plugin owns recipient policy.

options.title: Decline First-Class ACL
options.body: Keep explicit operator sends unrestricted under the trusted-operator model and document prompt/tool/plugin workarounds for deployments that want extra hardening.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack `allowSendTo`/`dmAllowTo`
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in Slack recipient allowlist that preserves current behavior when unset and is enforced in the Slack send path with docs and tests.
